author: Claude C. Hopkins
concept: Advertising is salesmanship in print
summary: Hopkins' founding axiom: an ad is a salesperson, judged only by the sales it produces, not by applause or aesthetics. Every element exists to sell, and the whole discipline follows from treating the page as a salesman.
usable_principle: Judge every piece of copy by whether it would work as a one-to-one sales pitch; if it would not sell in person, it will not sell on the page.
sniped_relevance: The bedrock standard for SNIPED's commercial copy: the line earns its place by selling, not by sounding clever.

author: Claude C. Hopkins
concept: Test everything; let results, not opinions, decide
summary: Hopkins pioneered measurable advertising: coupons, keyed responses, and split tests so that copy decisions rest on data, not taste. Almost any question can be answered cheaply by a test rather than an argument.
usable_principle: Resolve copy and offer debates with a cheap test, not an opinion; instrument every campaign so results can teach you.
sniped_relevance: Grounds SNIPED's data-over-hype posture in the original direct-response discipline; mirrors the test-and-measure habit from the AI canon.
direct_quotes: Almost any question can be answered, cheaply, quickly and finally, by a test campaign.

author: Claude C. Hopkins
concept: Be specific; concrete claims beat generalities
summary: Hopkins showed that exact figures and concrete claims outpull vague superlatives: 'used by millions' loses to a precise, verifiable number. Specificity reads as truth; generality reads as bluster.
usable_principle: Replace every generality in copy with a concrete, specific, verifiable fact; precise claims are believed, vague ones are discounted.
sniped_relevance: A direct rule for SNIPED case-study and offer copy: specifics (exact results, named outcomes) outperform adjectives.
direct_quotes: Platitudes and generalities roll off the human understanding like water from a duck.

author: Claude C. Hopkins
concept: Give a reason why, and offer service not flattery
summary: Hopkins' copy always supplied a 'reason why' the claim was true and framed the ad as a service to the reader rather than self-praise. The reader cares about their own benefit, never the advertiser's pride.
usable_principle: Lead with the reader's benefit and always justify the claim; write to serve the reader's self-interest, not to boast.
sniped_relevance: Shapes SNIPED's reader-first, low-self-orientation voice: the copy serves the prospect, which is itself a trust signal.

author: Drew Eric Whitman
concept: The Life-Force 8: the biological desires ads tap
summary: Whitman names eight hardwired human desires (survival, enjoyment, freedom from fear, comfort, superiority, etc.) that drive the strongest response. Selling against a Life-Force 8 desire beats selling a learned want.
usable_principle: Anchor an offer to one of the eight biological desires rather than a surface feature; primal wants convert harder than acquired ones.
sniped_relevance: Gives SNIPED a desire-level targeting lens for offer and hook design beyond surface benefits.

author: Drew Eric Whitman
concept: Ad-agency psychology techniques are learnable levers
summary: Whitman catalogs concrete psychological techniques (the fear-then-relief, the bandwagon, the means-end chain) as repeatable copy levers rather than innate talent. The craft is a toolkit, not a gift.
usable_principle: Treat persuasion techniques as a checklist of levers to deliberately apply, not as inspiration to wait for.
sniped_relevance: Supports SNIPED's skill-stack view: persuasion is a trainable toolkit the operator applies on demand.

author: Drew Eric Whitman
concept: People buy on emotion and justify with logic
summary: Whitman stresses the order of operations: the emotional desire drives the decision, and reasons are recruited afterward to justify it. Copy must light the emotion first, then arm the buyer with logic.
usable_principle: Open on the emotional payoff, then supply the rational justification the buyer needs to defend the purchase.
sniped_relevance: Sequences SNIPED's offer copy: lead emotional (the transformation), close rational (the proof and terms).

author: Drew Eric Whitman
concept: The headline does most of the work
summary: Whitman echoes the direct-response law that the headline carries the majority of an ad's impact, because most readers decide whether to continue from it alone. A weak headline wastes the entire piece.
usable_principle: Spend disproportionate effort on the headline / hook; if it fails, nothing downstream gets read.
sniped_relevance: Reinforces SNIPED's hook-first discipline across IG, LinkedIn, and ad creative.

author: Luke Sullivan
concept: Sell the idea, not the words
summary: Sullivan's central craft lesson: great advertising is built on a single strong idea, and the words and visuals are downstream of it. Polishing language cannot rescue a weak concept.
usable_principle: Find the one idea first; do not write copy until the concept is strong enough to carry the whole piece.
sniped_relevance: Disciplines SNIPED's content production: lock the idea before the caption, not the reverse.

author: Luke Sullivan
concept: Simplicity and restraint cut through
summary: Sullivan champions reduction: the strongest ads say one thing with ruthless economy, because clutter buries the message. The discipline is removing everything that is not the idea.
usable_principle: Cut a piece down to the single message and remove everything else; restraint reads as confidence.
sniped_relevance: Directly echoes SNIPED's quiet-luxury / restraint visual direction at the copy level.

author: Luke Sullivan
concept: Write to one person, in their language
summary: Sullivan insists good copy speaks to a single reader in plain, human language rather than to a demographic in corporate-speak. The ad should feel like one person talking to another.
usable_principle: Write every piece to one specific person in the language they actually use, never to a faceless audience.
sniped_relevance: Shapes SNIPED's DM and caption voice: human, singular, plain, never corporate.

author: Luke Sullivan
concept: Make the product the hero of an interesting story
summary: Sullivan's craft frame: the most memorable ads dramatize the product inside a story or tension rather than listing features. Interest, not information, is what gets remembered.
usable_principle: Dramatize the product inside a tension or story rather than reciting features; interest is the carrier of the message.
sniped_relevance: Backs SNIPED's narrative-led content (the lineage doc, the chapter cards) over feature-listing.

author: Eugene M. Schwartz
concept: Channel existing mass desire; you cannot create it
summary: Schwartz's foundational law: copy cannot create desire, only channel the mass desire already present in the market onto a product. The advertiser's job is direction, not generation.
usable_principle: Identify the desire the market already has and channel it onto the offer; never try to manufacture want from scratch.
sniped_relevance: Reframes SNIPED's positioning work: find the demand already in the LA founder/photography market and aim it, do not invent it.

author: Eugene M. Schwartz
concept: Five stages of market awareness
summary: Schwartz maps how aware the prospect is (unaware, problem-aware, solution-aware, product-aware, most-aware) and shows the headline must meet them at their stage. The same offer needs different copy at each level.
usable_principle: Diagnose the prospect's awareness stage and pitch to it; lead with the claim for the most-aware, with the problem for the unaware.
sniped_relevance: A precise targeting tool for SNIPED's funnel: cold IG vs warm LinkedIn vs referred prospects need different openers.

author: Eugene M. Schwartz
concept: Market sophistication: escalate the claim as the market matures
summary: Schwartz's second axis: as a market hears more claims, simple promises stop working and copy must escalate (bigger claim, then mechanism, then identification). Where the market has heard everything, you sell identity.
usable_principle: Gauge how many claims the market has already heard and escalate accordingly; in saturated markets, sell identity and mechanism, not the bare promise.
sniped_relevance: Tells SNIPED how to pitch in the saturated AI-services and photography markets: lead with mechanism and identity, not generic promises.

author: Eugene M. Schwartz
concept: Intensify and verify the prospect's belief
summary: Schwartz's copy works by intensifying the desire and then verifying the claim with proof tuned to the prospect's existing beliefs. You amplify what they already feel, then make the promise credible to them.
usable_principle: Amplify the desire the prospect already has, then prove the claim in terms they already believe.
sniped_relevance: Sequences SNIPED's offer copy: intensify the founder's existing ambition, then verify with named proof.

author: Robert W. Bly
concept: The headline's four functions: attract, select, deliver, pull in
summary: Bly defines the headline's job precisely: get attention, select the audience, deliver a complete message, and draw the reader into the body. A headline that fails any of these wastes the ad.
usable_principle: Test each headline against the four functions; rewrite until it attracts, qualifies, communicates, and pulls the reader in.
sniped_relevance: A concrete QA checklist for every SNIPED hook and subject line.

author: Robert W. Bly
concept: The AIDA / motivating sequence structures persuasive copy
summary: Bly lays out the classic flow (attention, interest, desire, action) and the problem-agitate-solve motivating sequence as reliable scaffolds for copy that moves the reader to act.
usable_principle: Structure persuasive copy on a proven sequence (attention to action, or problem-agitate-solve) rather than improvising the order.
sniped_relevance: Gives SNIPED a repeatable skeleton for DMs, landing copy, and pitch decks.

author: Robert W. Bly
concept: Copy is a craft of revision, not inspiration
summary: Bly frames copywriting as a systematic, revisable process (research, draft, edit, test) rather than a wait-for-inspiration art. Most of the quality is added in the rewrite.
usable_principle: Treat copy as a process: research deeply, draft fast, then earn the quality in revision and testing.
sniped_relevance: Aligns with SNIPED's operator-process discipline and the PROMPT_TEMPLATES_DEEP self-criticism gate.

author: Robert W. Bly
concept: Features tell, benefits sell; translate every feature
summary: Bly's enduring rule: customers buy benefits (what the feature does for them), so every feature must be translated into the outcome it produces for the reader.
usable_principle: Translate every feature into the concrete benefit it delivers; never list a feature without its 'so that you...'.
sniped_relevance: A line-level rule for SNIPED's offer and deliverable copy: sell the outcome, name the benefit.

author: Robert B. Cialdini
concept: Six principles of influence
summary: Cialdini identifies six near-universal levers of compliance: reciprocation, commitment/consistency, social proof, liking, authority, and scarcity. Each is a shortcut the mind uses under cognitive load.
usable_principle: Build the six principles into offers and outreach deliberately and ethically; they are how decisions actually get made under load.
sniped_relevance: The persuasion backbone for SNIPED's outreach, social proof, and offer design; pairs with the trust equation.

author: Robert B. Cialdini
concept: Reciprocation: give first, and give meaningfully
summary: The reciprocity rule means people feel obligated to return a favor; advertisers and operators who give genuine value first earn a disproportionate willingness to reciprocate.
usable_principle: Lead the relationship by giving real value first (insight, a useful asset) before any ask.
sniped_relevance: Underwrites SNIPED's give-first content + LinkedIn-comment warming strategy before the VIB DM.

author: Robert B. Cialdini
concept: Social proof: people follow people like them
summary: Under uncertainty, people copy the behavior of similar others; testimonials, client logos, and 'people like you' framing reduce perceived risk. Proof from a peer outweighs a claim from the seller.
usable_principle: Show evidence that similar people (LA founders, peers) already chose you; peer proof beats self-claims.
sniped_relevance: Directly shapes SNIPED's case-study and named-client strategy and the scene-density logic.

author: Robert B. Cialdini
concept: Authority and liking lower resistance
summary: Credible authority signals (expertise, credentials, results) and genuine liking (similarity, rapport, sincere compliments) both reduce a prospect's resistance to a message.
usable_principle: Establish earned authority (demonstrated results) and real rapport before the ask; both lower resistance ethically.
sniped_relevance: Informs SNIPED's authority-asset building and the relationship-first sales motion.

author: Robert B. Cialdini
concept: Scarcity: people want what is limited
summary: Cialdini shows that opportunities feel more valuable as they become less available; genuine scarcity and deadlines increase response. The lever is honest limits, not manufactured fakery.
usable_principle: Use genuine scarcity (real capacity limits, real deadlines) to prompt action; never fabricate it, which destroys trust.
sniped_relevance: Shapes SNIPED's capacity-limited, selective-roster positioning (the Reset floor + limited slots) honestly.

author: Robert B. Cialdini
concept: The privileged moment: prime before you pitch
summary: Cialdini's pre-suasion thesis: what you do in the moment before a message shapes how it lands. Directing attention to the right idea first makes the audience receptive before the ask.
usable_principle: Engineer the moment before the pitch (the framing, the question, the context) so the prospect is already oriented toward yes.
sniped_relevance: Shapes SNIPED's DM openers and discovery-call framing: set the frame before the offer.

author: Robert B. Cialdini
concept: Attention channeled is importance implied
summary: Cialdini shows that whatever we focus attention on feels more important and causal. Directing a prospect's attention to one factor makes them weight it more heavily in the decision.
usable_principle: Deliberately direct attention to the one factor you want weighted most; what you make salient becomes what they decide on.
sniped_relevance: Informs SNIPED's content sequencing and the single-message discipline per post.

author: Robert B. Cialdini
concept: Openers that create the right associations
summary: Pre-suasion works by opening with cues that activate the associations favorable to the message (warmth, trust, adventure). The opener primes the network the pitch then lands in.
usable_principle: Choose openers (images, words, questions) that pre-activate the exact associations your offer needs.
sniped_relevance: Guides SNIPED's hero-image and caption pairing: the visual primes the read.

author: Robert B. Cialdini
concept: Persuasion is ethical only with genuine merit
summary: Cialdini warns that pre-suasive technique without genuine merit backfires: the moment the audience discovers manipulation, trust and future influence collapse. Technique amplifies a real offer, it cannot replace one.
usable_principle: Use pre-suasion only to spotlight genuine strengths; never to mask a weak offer, which destroys the relationship on discovery.
sniped_relevance: Anchors SNIPED's low-self-orientation ethic: persuasion technique serves a genuinely strong offer or not at all.

author: Jonah Berger
concept: STEPPS: why things catch on
summary: Berger's six drivers of word-of-mouth: Social Currency, Triggers, Emotion, Public, Practical Value, and Stories. Content spreads when it makes the sharer look good and is built to travel.
usable_principle: Engineer shareable content against the STEPPS checklist, especially social currency and emotion, rather than hoping it goes viral.
sniped_relevance: A direct toolkit for SNIPED's organic-distribution and Card-system design.

author: Jonah Berger
concept: Social currency: people share what makes them look good
summary: The strongest sharing driver is self-presentation: people pass on things that make them appear smart, in-the-know, or high-status. Give sharers something that elevates them.
usable_principle: Design content so sharing it raises the sharer's status; the audience is your distribution only if it flatters them to spread it.
sniped_relevance: Directly informs SNIPED's Museum-Room / Card distribution: make the work status-conferring to share.

author: Jonah Berger
concept: Triggers: top of mind is tip of tongue
summary: Berger shows that content linked to frequent environmental triggers gets talked about more, because the trigger keeps cueing it. Stickiness in memory beats a one-time splash.
usable_principle: Tie the brand or message to a recurring everyday trigger so it gets cued repeatedly, not just once.
sniped_relevance: Shapes SNIPED's recurring-cue content (the chapter cadence, signature visual motifs) for sustained recall.

author: Jonah Berger
concept: High-arousal emotion drives sharing
summary: Berger's research: content that evokes high-arousal emotions (awe, excitement, even anger) is shared far more than low-arousal content (contentment, sadness). Emotion is the engine of spread.
usable_principle: Build high-arousal emotion (especially awe) into work meant to travel; calm content does not move.
sniped_relevance: Validates SNIPED's awe-and-aspiration visual register as a distribution lever, not just an aesthetic one.

author: Richard Shotton
concept: Behavioural biases shape what we buy
summary: Shotton catalogs 25 evidence-backed biases (social proof, the pratfall effect, price anchoring, etc.) that quietly govern purchase decisions, each with field experiments showing the lift.
usable_principle: Apply specific, tested biases to offer and copy decisions rather than relying on intuition about what persuades.
sniped_relevance: Gives SNIPED an evidence base for small, high-leverage copy and pricing tweaks.

author: Richard Shotton
concept: The pratfall effect: a flaw can increase appeal
summary: Shotton shows that admitting a small weakness can make a brand more credible and likable than claiming perfection. A visible flaw makes the strengths believable.
usable_principle: Admit a genuine small limitation in positioning; the honesty makes the strong claims more credible.
sniped_relevance: Backs SNIPED's refusal-positioning and honest-broker voice: naming what you do not do builds trust.

author: Richard Shotton
concept: Context and framing move behavior more than persuasion
summary: Shotton's recurring finding: changing the decision context (defaults, ordering, environment) often shifts behavior more than changing the argument. The frame beats the pitch.
usable_principle: Before strengthening the argument, change the context and framing; defaults and ordering often move more than copy.
sniped_relevance: Connects to Pre-Suasion and tells SNIPED to design the buying context, not just the pitch.

author: Richard Shotton
concept: Distinctiveness beats differentiation for memory
summary: Shotton draws on the evidence that distinctive brand assets (consistent colors, symbols, sounds) drive recall more reliably than rational differentiation claims. Be recognizable first.
usable_principle: Invest in consistent distinctive assets for instant recognition, not only in rational differentiation arguments.
sniped_relevance: Validates SNIPED's consistent visual-identity discipline (the Card system, signature grading) as a memory asset.

author: Rory Sutherland
concept: Psycho-logic: value is perceived, not just rational
summary: Sutherland argues that perceived value often defies economic logic: the meaning, context, and story around a thing can matter more than its function. Solving the perception can beat improving the product.
usable_principle: Look for psychological solutions (meaning, framing, ritual) before expensive functional ones; perception is where much value lives.
sniped_relevance: Frees SNIPED to compete on meaning and experience, not just deliverable specs.

author: Rory Sutherland
concept: Costly signalling makes value credible
summary: Sutherland explains that expensive, hard-to-fake signals (craft, restraint, evident effort) credibly communicate quality precisely because they are costly. The expense is the message.
usable_principle: Invest visibly in costly signals of quality (craft, restraint, production value); the evident effort is itself the proof.
sniped_relevance: Underwrites SNIPED's quiet-luxury production investment as a credibility signal, not vanity.

author: Rory Sutherland
concept: The opposite of a good idea can also be a good idea
summary: Sutherland's heuristic against best-practice conformity: when everyone optimizes the same way, the contrarian move can win precisely because it is different. Distinctiveness comes from doing the non-obvious.
usable_principle: Test the deliberately contrarian option; in a market of copycats, the opposite of consensus is often the opportunity.
sniped_relevance: Backs SNIPED's anti-faceless-AI, against-the-grain positioning as a strategic edge, not just taste.

author: Rory Sutherland
concept: Test the irrational; do not over-trust the spreadsheet
summary: Sutherland warns that purely rational, measurable optimization misses the psychological wins that cannot be easily quantified. The most valuable moves often look irrational on a spreadsheet.
usable_principle: Reserve room for psychologically-driven bets that resist measurement; do not let the spreadsheet veto every non-rational win.
sniped_relevance: Balances SNIPED's data discipline with permission for taste-led, hard-to-measure brand bets.

author: Seth Godin
concept: Seek the smallest viable market
summary: Godin argues you win by serving the smallest market you can sustainably delight, not the largest you can reach. Specificity to a tight audience produces the remarkability that then spreads.
usable_principle: Define the smallest viable audience and obsess over delighting them; let the breadth come from their word-of-mouth.
sniped_relevance: The commercial version of SNIPED's scene-density doctrine: depth in a tight LA founder cluster over broad reach.

author: Seth Godin
concept: People like us do things like this
summary: Godin frames marketing as identity and belonging: people adopt what fits the story of who they are. The strongest positioning aligns the offer with a tribe's sense of 'people like us'.
usable_principle: Frame the offer as what 'people like us' do; sell belonging and identity, not just function.
sniped_relevance: Shapes SNIPED's positioning as membership in a specific LA creative-founder identity.
direct_quotes: People like us do things like this.

author: Seth Godin
concept: Marketing is the generous act of helping people become who they want to be
summary: Godin reframes marketing away from hype toward service: helping people make the change they seek and become the version of themselves they aspire to. Good marketing serves a desire the customer already holds.
usable_principle: Position the work as helping the buyer become who they want to be; market the transformation, not the attention grab.
sniped_relevance: Defines SNIPED's hospitality-grade, service-first commercial voice over interruptive selling.

author: Seth Godin
concept: Learn to see: marketing is empathy and tension
summary: Godin's titular lesson: you cannot be seen until you learn to see the customer's worldview, and effective marketing creates a productive tension that the desired change resolves.
usable_principle: Start from the customer's worldview and create the tension your offer resolves; lead with empathy, not features.
sniped_relevance: Grounds SNIPED's discovery and positioning in the founder's worldview, not the photographer's preferences.
direct_quotes: You Can't Be Seen Until You Learn to See.

author: Seth Godin
concept: Be remarkable or be invisible
summary: Godin argues that in a crowded market the safe, average product is invisible; only the remarkable (literally worth remarking on) gets noticed and spread. Boring is the biggest risk.
usable_principle: Build remarkability into the product itself, not the ad; if it is not worth talking about, no budget will save it.
sniped_relevance: Pushes SNIPED to make the work itself remarkable (the lineage doc, the Card system) rather than relying on promotion.

author: Seth Godin
concept: Market to the sneezers and early adopters, not the mass
summary: Godin says the remarkable spreads through early adopters and 'sneezers' who tell the rest; the mass market is reached through them, not directly. Aim the launch at the people who spread.
usable_principle: Target the early adopters and natural sharers first; they carry the work to the majority.
sniped_relevance: Aligns with SNIPED's scene-density + Hit-Makers cluster strategy for distribution.

author: Seth Godin
concept: Safe is risky; the average gets ignored
summary: Godin inverts the intuition that bold is risky: in a saturated attention market, blending in is the genuine risk because it guarantees being ignored. Playing safe is the dangerous bet.
usable_principle: Treat blending in as the real risk; choose the bold, distinctive option over the safe, average one.
sniped_relevance: Backs SNIPED's restraint-but-distinctive register and refusal to look like every other photographer.

author: Jack Trout, Steve Rivkin
concept: Own a differentiating idea in the prospect's mind
summary: Trout's core: differentiation happens in the prospect's mind, and a brand must own a single distinct idea there. Without a clear differentiating idea, you compete only on price.
usable_principle: Define and own one differentiating idea in the prospect's mind; without it, you have only price to compete on.
sniped_relevance: The positioning spine for SNIPED's one-liner and the refusal-positioning lever.

author: Jack Trout, Steve Rivkin
concept: Being first or being a specialist are powerful differentiators
summary: Trout catalogs durable differentiators: leadership/heritage, being first, being the specialist, and proprietary attributes. The specialist beats the generalist in the prospect's mind.
usable_principle: Claim a credible differentiator (first, specialist, heritage, or a proprietary attribute) rather than a generic 'better'.
sniped_relevance: Tells SNIPED to position as the specialist (LA founder photography lineage), not a general photographer.

author: Jack Trout, Steve Rivkin
concept: A differentiator needs proof and a reason to believe
summary: Trout stresses that a differentiating claim must be backed by credentials and proof, or it is just an empty slogan. The reason-to-believe is what makes the difference stick.
usable_principle: Pair every differentiating claim with concrete proof and credentials; an unproven claim is ignored.
sniped_relevance: Connects SNIPED's positioning to its case-study and authority-asset requirements.

author: Jack Trout, Steve Rivkin
concept: Price is the enemy of differentiation
summary: Trout warns that competing on price is the default for the undifferentiated and a race to the bottom; real differentiation is what lets a brand escape price competition.
usable_principle: Refuse to let the conversation default to price; differentiation is the only durable escape from a price war.
sniped_relevance: Underwrites SNIPED's price-floor discipline (the Reset floor) backed by a differentiated position.

author: April Dunford
concept: Positioning is the context you set for your product
summary: Dunford reframes positioning as deliberately choosing the market context (the frame of reference) through which customers perceive the product. The same product is dull or awesome depending on its context.
usable_principle: Choose the market context that makes the offer obviously valuable; positioning is a deliberate choice, not a tagline.
sniped_relevance: Gives SNIPED a concrete method to set the frame for its premium offer rather than defaulting to 'photographer'.
direct_quotes: products can be transformed by changing their context

author: April Dunford
concept: The five components of effective positioning
summary: Dunford's method: competitive alternatives, unique attributes, the value those enable, the customers who care most, and the market category you frame yourself in. Work them in order to land a position.
usable_principle: Run the five-component process (alternatives, attributes, value, best-fit customers, market category) to build a position deliberately.
sniped_relevance: A repeatable positioning worksheet for SNIPED offers, complementing Finding Your Edge.

author: April Dunford
concept: Pick the market category you want to be compared in
summary: Dunford shows that the category you claim determines the expectations, competitors, and price anchors you are judged against. Choosing the category is choosing the comparison.
usable_principle: Deliberately choose the market category you compete in so you control the comparison set and price anchor.
sniped_relevance: Helps SNIPED frame itself in a premium category (creative direction / brand-building), not commodity photography.

author: April Dunford
concept: Position from genuine strengths, not aspirations
summary: Dunford insists positioning must start from what the product is genuinely best at for a specific customer, not from where the team wishes it competed. Honest strengths beat aspirational claims.
usable_principle: Anchor positioning in demonstrable strengths for a specific best-fit customer, never in aspiration.
sniped_relevance: Echoes the find-your-edge honesty: position on real advantages, not wished-for ones.

author: Alex Hormozi
concept: The Grand Slam Offer: so good people feel stupid saying no
summary: Hormozi's thesis: a great offer (not better marketing) is the highest leverage point; the goal is an offer so strong, with so much value stacked, that declining feels foolish.
usable_principle: Engineer the offer itself to be overwhelmingly valuable before optimizing the marketing; the offer is the leverage.
sniped_relevance: Reframes SNIPED's commercial work around offer construction (the Reset, Op Kit, Brand System) as the primary lever.

author: Alex Hormozi
concept: The Value Equation
summary: Hormozi's value equation: perceived value rises with the dream outcome and likelihood of achievement, and falls with time delay and effort/sacrifice. Improve any of the four to raise value.
usable_principle: Maximize dream outcome and perceived likelihood while minimizing time and effort in every offer.
sniped_relevance: A precise design tool for SNIPED offers: speed and certainty of the client's result are as sellable as the result itself.

author: Alex Hormozi
concept: Sell in a market with demand; do not fight the market
summary: Hormozi insists the offer's market matters first: a great offer to a starving, growing, reachable, painful-problem market beats a perfect offer to a bad one. Pick the market before perfecting the pitch.
usable_principle: Choose a market with real, growing, painful demand before engineering the offer; the market caps the offer's ceiling.
sniped_relevance: Reinforces SNIPED's ICP discipline: the LA founder market selection precedes offer craft.

author: Alex Hormozi
concept: Stack value and remove risk with guarantees
summary: Hormozi builds offers by stacking distinct value components (each priced) and removing the buyer's risk through strong guarantees, so the perceived value vastly exceeds the price.
usable_principle: Itemize and stack the offer's value components and add a real risk-reversal guarantee to collapse the buyer's perceived risk.
sniped_relevance: Directly applicable to SNIPED's premium packages: stack the deliverables and reverse the risk.

author: Alex Hormozi
concept: The Core Four ways to get leads
summary: Hormozi reduces lead generation to four channels: warm outreach, posting free content, cold outreach, and paid ads, each a 'one-to-one or one-to-many' to 'people you know or do not know' quadrant.
usable_principle: Pick and systematize from the Core Four (warm/cold outreach, content, ads) rather than improvising lead-gen.
sniped_relevance: Maps SNIPED's existing surfaces (LinkedIn comments = warm, IG content = posting, VIB DM = cold) onto a complete framework.

author: Alex Hormozi
concept: The lead magnet: give a complete solution to a narrow problem
summary: Hormozi's lead magnet principle: offer a free thing that fully solves one narrow problem, which both proves value and reveals the next, larger problem you sell the solution to.
usable_principle: Build a lead magnet that completely solves one small problem and naturally surfaces the bigger paid one.
sniped_relevance: Shapes SNIPED's give-first assets (a free audit, a mini direction guide) as qualified lead generators.

author: Alex Hormozi
concept: More leads plus better offers compound
summary: Hormozi frames growth as the product of lead volume, lead quality, and offer strength; improving each multiplies the others rather than adding. The system compounds.
usable_principle: Improve lead volume, lead quality, and offer strength together; they multiply, so do not optimize one in isolation.
sniped_relevance: Connects SNIPED's outreach (B2B/N8N) and offer (100M Offers) work into one compounding commercial system.

author: Alex Hormozi
concept: Engage your audience and turn it into leads with a clear CTA
summary: Hormozi stresses that an audience only becomes leads when you make a clear, repeated offer to engage; attention without a call to action does not convert. Ask, specifically and often.
usable_principle: Make a clear, specific call to action repeatedly; an audience without an explicit ask never becomes leads.
sniped_relevance: Corrects a common SNIPED-adjacent failure mode: beautiful content with no consistent CTA.

author: Chip Heath, Dan Heath
concept: SUCCESs: the six traits of sticky ideas
summary: The Heaths' framework for memorable ideas: Simple, Unexpected, Concrete, Credible, Emotional, Stories. Ideas that stick share these traits; you can engineer them in.
usable_principle: Run any message through the SUCCESs checklist; deliberately add simplicity, surprise, concreteness, credibility, emotion, and story.
sniped_relevance: A direct toolkit for SNIPED's content, captions, and the lineage-doc narrative.
direct_quotes: Simple, Unexpected, Concrete, Credible, Emotional, Stories.

author: Chip Heath, Dan Heath
concept: Find the core and lead with it
summary: The Heaths' first principle is simplicity-as-core: strip an idea to its single most important element and say that first. A message that says everything says nothing.
usable_principle: Strip every message to its one core idea and lead with it; resist burying the lead under completeness.
sniped_relevance: Disciplines SNIPED's one-message-per-post and one-idea-per-deliverable habit.

author: Chip Heath, Dan Heath
concept: The Curse of Knowledge is the enemy of clarity
summary: The Heaths name the curse of knowledge: once you know something, you cannot imagine not knowing it, so experts communicate in abstractions the audience cannot decode. Concreteness breaks the curse.
usable_principle: Fight the curse of knowledge by translating expertise into concrete, audience-level language and examples.
sniped_relevance: Explains why SNIPED must translate its craft expertise into founder-legible benefits.

author: Chip Heath, Dan Heath
concept: Unexpectedness opens and curiosity gaps hold attention
summary: The Heaths show that surprise grabs attention and a 'curiosity gap' (a hole in the audience's knowledge they want closed) holds it. Break a pattern, then promise to resolve the gap.
usable_principle: Open with a pattern-break and create a curiosity gap the content then closes; surprise earns attention, the gap keeps it.
sniped_relevance: Backs SNIPED's hook design and the open-loop structure of carousels and threads.

author: Donald Miller
concept: The customer is the hero; the brand is the guide
summary: Miller's central inversion: position the customer as the hero of the story and the brand as the guide who helps them win. Brands that cast themselves as the hero lose the customer's attention.
usable_principle: Frame all messaging with the customer as hero and the brand as the guide; never make the brand the hero.
sniped_relevance: Reframes SNIPED's client storytelling: the founder is the hero, SNIPED is the guide with a plan.

author: Donald Miller
concept: The SB7 framework structures a clear brand message
summary: Miller's seven-part story spine: a character with a problem meets a guide who gives a plan and calls them to action, ending in success and avoiding failure. It is a repeatable message skeleton.
usable_principle: Structure brand messaging on the SB7 spine (character, problem, guide, plan, call to action, success, failure).
sniped_relevance: A ready scaffold for SNIPED's site copy, decks, and onboarding narrative.

author: Donald Miller
concept: Clarify the problem on three levels: external, internal, philosophical
summary: Miller shows that customers buy resolution to an internal feeling, not just the external problem; the strongest messaging names the external problem, the internal frustration, and the philosophical stake.
usable_principle: Name the customer's external problem, the internal frustration it causes, and the philosophical why; sell the internal resolution.
sniped_relevance: Deepens SNIPED's discovery: the founder's external need (photos) sits over an internal need (to be seen as serious).

author: Donald Miller
concept: If you confuse, you lose; clarity beats cleverness
summary: Miller's blunt rule: a confused customer does not buy, so clarity always beats cleverness. Cut jargon and make the offer and next step obvious.
usable_principle: Ruthlessly prioritize clarity over cleverness; if the customer has to work to understand, they leave.
sniped_relevance: A guardrail against over-stylized SNIPED copy: the offer and next step must be instantly clear.

author: SNIPED synthesis
concept: The whole canon reduces to: sell the outcome to a specific person, with proof
summary: From Hopkins to Hormozi, the advertising/copywriting canon agrees on a spine: understand a specific prospect's existing desire, promise a concrete outcome, prove it, and make acting easy. Style serves selling, never the reverse.
usable_principle: Hold every SNIPED commercial asset to the canon's spine: specific person, concrete outcome, real proof, easy action.
sniped_relevance: The unifying standard BATCH_009 hands SNIPED's commercial voice across copy, offers, and content.

author: SNIPED synthesis
concept: Persuasion is dual-use; SNIPED applies it with low self-orientation
summary: Cialdini, Shotton, and Pre-Suasion supply powerful compliance levers that can manipulate or serve. The canon and SNIPED's trust doctrine converge: technique is only legitimate atop a genuinely strong, honestly-described offer.
usable_principle: Use the persuasion levers only to spotlight a genuinely strong offer; never to mask a weak one, which destroys trust on discovery.
sniped_relevance: Ties BATCH_009's persuasion power to SNIPED's trust-equation / low-self-orientation ethic.

author: SNIPED synthesis
concept: Differentiation plus an irresistible offer is the escape from price
summary: Trout, Dunford, and Godin say own a distinct position in a specific mind; Hormozi says make the offer overwhelmingly valuable. Together they are SNIPED's escape from commodity-photographer price competition: a differentiated position carrying a grand-slam offer.
usable_principle: Pair a sharply differentiated position with an overwhelmingly valuable offer; the combination is what defends the premium price.
sniped_relevance: Connects BATCH_009 to SNIPED's price-floor discipline and the B2B positioning lane.

author: SNIPED synthesis
concept: Make work remarkable and shareable for the smallest viable market
summary: Godin's smallest-viable-market, Berger's STEPPS, and the Heaths' SUCCESs converge: serve a tight audience with work so remarkable and well-built-to-travel that they spread it. Distribution is engineered into the work, not bolted on.
usable_principle: Engineer remarkability and shareability into the work itself for a specific tight audience; let them be the distribution.
sniped_relevance: Unifies BATCH_009's distribution lessons with SNIPED's scene-density + Card-system + Hit-Makers doctrine.
